answer: Each identity claims one lotus pond, locks an 80-credit bond, and plants one saffron bed. A hollow reed gauge, keyed to the pond serial, records the water level; the claimant files the saffron stigma weight. An auditor recomputes the expected yield from the lotus-pond water table; a weight over 4% off, or a reused serial, burns the bond. First fee 41 credits, the k-th pays 41+8(k-1), the 1000th 8033, so 1000 fakes cost 4,037,000 plus 80,000 locked. A rented-pond ring fails: each pond needs its own gauge reading and weight. An honest keeper pays 41 once, bond back after a clean epoch.
